AFCorsair_CSRB4t3.overview: The compact laser system and sleek design of the Corsair made it a superior aerospace fighter in an atmosphere, rivaling the capabilities of Conventional Fighters.
AFCorsair_CSRB4t3.capabilities: It was well protected by thirteen and a half tons of armor, while sixteen heat sinks kept the all-energy weapon loadout from overheating. It carried a fuel load of five tons and its GM 200 power plant could achieve a maximum thrust of four and a half gravities, with a safe thrust factor of three gravities.
AFCorsair_CSRB4t3.history: The Corsair was originally introduced as a means to replace the horrific losses suffered by the Star League Defense Force following the end of the Amaris Civil War. A working prototype of the Corsair had already been produced when the SLDF approached Wangker Aerospace for an easy-to-refit Aerospace Fighter, which allowed them to begin full-scale production within months. Unfortunately the original V1 series had serious flaws: the fuel tank would rupture when the craft made turns operating in an atmosphere, the landing gear could not support its weight in an emergency landing, and the life support system in the cockpit was easily shattered. While such faults would have killed most other designs, the positive aspects of the Corsair were so impressive the Star League permitted its continuation while Wangker fixed the issues. The fuel tank problem would be corrected in the V2 series, while the life support issues were hashed out in the V3 through V8 series, with continuing improvements up to the V12 series. Most of Wangker's Corsair factories were located in the Federated Suns, and so when the Star League fell five years after its introduction House Davion managed to seize control of them, with the Free Worlds League capturing a single production line on Connaught. Within five years of the start of the First Succession War however all of these factories had been destroyed, though through salvage efforts Wangker managed to piece together a new line on Axton and keep it open over the centuries of constant raiding. When the Connaught facility was destroyed in the opening shots of the war only a few hundred had been produced for the FWLM, and these eventually fell into the hands of the Principality of Regulus. When the Federated Commonwealth was formed debate raged on whether the Corsair or the Lucifer should be the AFFC's standard medium fighter, and in mock combat trials the Corsair won more often than not.
AFCorsair_CSRB4t3.deployment: Geared towards short range combat, the Corsair carries a total of two Martell Medium Lasers and four ExoStar Small Lasers, while two ExoStar Large Lasers gives it some additional reach. Both medium lasers are located in each wing, with the large lasers and two of the small lasers filling the nose. For coverage to the stern, the remaining two small lasers are mounted to the rear and tied directly into the targeting systems, giving the pilot extreme accuracy in his rear field of fire. The compact laser systems are also well-suited for a ground-attack role, while the presence of sixteen heat sinks means the Corsair can continuously fire both large lasers and fire the medium and small lasers with negligible heat buildup.

AFShilone_SL17BATLCOS.overview: The SL-17 Shilone is Wakazashi Enterprises' signature medium aerospace fighter, designed to meet the Draconis Combine's urgent need for a capable and resilient interceptor at the dawn of the Succession Wars. Built at Chatham, the Shilone quickly earned a reputation as a genuine overperformer in its weight class, fielding heavy firepower and substantial armor coverage more typical of fighters in heavier tonnage brackets. Nicknamed "The Boomerang" by its pilots for its remarkable habit of returning from even heavily contested engagements, it became a mainstay of the Draconis Combine Aerospace Force, eventually spreading through licensing agreements to the Outworlds Alliance and the Taurian Concordat. Pilots from every nation who have had occasion to fly the Shilone typically come away with a high regard for its combat reliability and well-balanced design.
AFShilone_SL17BATLCOS.capabilities:
The Shilone carries a weapons loadout weighted toward long-range engagement. Its nose-mounted Shigunga LRM rack allows pilots to pound targets before closing to visual range, while a Diverse Optics large laser provides a heat-efficient complement to the missile barrage. Two wing-mounted medium lasers extend the fighter's effectiveness once inside effective missile range, and a rear-facing NCK short-range missile launcher discourages pursuit. The combination yields a fighter capable of effective engagement across nearly every range band, though the Shilone performs best when pilots leverage its long-range punch to wear down enemies before transitioning to close-quarters fire.

Mass tactics are common among Shilone squadrons, with entire flights coordinating concentrated missile salvos onto a single target before breaking into individual engagements. Against other aerospace fighters this approach is moderately effective, but against DropShips or orbital installations the concentrated fire can be devastating. The Shilone carries heavier armor than most fighters of comparable mass, lending it staying power that lighter designs lack. Its pilot entry hatch is unconventionally located on the belly rather than the canopy, a quirk that has not affected operational effectiveness but frequently surprises new crew. Twenty single heat sinks handle the energy load adequately, though sustained simultaneous use of the full weapon suite generates heat levels that demand pilot discipline.
AFShilone_SL17BATLCOS.history:
The Shilone's origins trace to the chaos of the First Succession War, when Wakazashi Enterprises found itself facing a key choice. As the Inner Sphere tore itself apart, Wakazashi's leadership announced plans to relocate operations to the relative safety of the Periphery. Coordinator Minoru Kurita moved quickly to prevent this, offering the company a substantial defense contract to stay and design a new medium fighter. The result was the Shilone, purpose-built to give the Combine a decisive edge in aerospace superiority battles.

The new fighter entered service during the First Succession War, with an early and little-publicized engagement at Barlow's Folly in 2786 marking its actual battlefield debut. That action ended without distinction, and later official accounts quietly omitted the date; the system's prior name of Cussar was likewise dropped from revised records. The Shilone's public reputation instead took shape at Kentares IV in 2796, where concentrated missile salvos from entire Shilone squadrons disrupted Davion aerospace formations before they could mount effective interception screens, allowing Combine DropShips to reach orbit and land their ground forces with minimal interference. That success established the massed long-range strike as the type's defining tactic.

The early production run was not without problems. In 2799, engineers discovered a structural defect in the wing joint assemblies of the original SL-17 models, a flaw responsible for several fatal crashes. Wakazashi moved aggressively to address the problem, and by 2802 all operational Shilones had been rebuilt with improved wing joints. The redesigned structure eliminated the issue entirely, and no structural failures have been reported since.

By the late Succession Wars period the Shilone's reputation was firmly established, and demand extended well beyond Combine borders. Wakazashi licensed production to the Outworlds Alliance in the 3020s, with the United Outworlders Corporation on Ramora taking up manufacture for Alliance aerospace forces. Both the Chatham and Ramora facilities subsequently entered long-term supply agreements with the Taurian Concordat, giving that state access to one of the Inner Sphere's most respected medium fighters. Pilots across every operating nation called the Shilone "a queen among aerospace fighters" and took personal pride in flying a machine that consistently outperformed its weight class.

The Ronin War of 3034 put Shilone squadrons in the skies over the newly independent Free Rasalhague Republic, where the fighter saw heavy use in the aerospace engagements that characterized that conflict. It was during this period that the type became closely identified with the Flying Drakøns, the aerospace wing of the First Rasalhague Drakøns, whose crews flew Shilones with exceptional skill and dedication. When the Clan Invasion began in 3050, those same pilots would write the Shilone's most defining chapter.

On 31 October 3050, the invasion reached a turning point above Radstadt. Elected Prince Haakon Magnusson and his escort, fleeing ahead of advancing Clan forces, jumped into the Radstadt system unaware that Clan Wolf had just completed its conquest of the planet. Aboard the Wolf flagship Dire Wolf, ilKhan Leo Showers had convened a Grand Kurultai to censure Clan Wolf's rapid advance. The Flying Drakøns immediately deployed to buy the Elected Prince time to escape, making repeated attack runs on the massive WarShip while Clan fighters scrambled to respond. The Drakøns took heavy losses in the exchange, and as the Prince's JumpShip finally broke free of the system, many of the surviving fighters were badly damaged. Kapten Tyra Miraborg found herself at the controls of a stricken Shilone, bleeding from multiple wounds, her fighter barely responding. Rather than withdraw, she disengaged all engine restraints and guided the crippled machine directly into the bridge of the Dire Wolf. The impact killed ilKhan Showers and devastated the flagship, ending the Grand Kurultai and leaving the Clans without a unifying leader at a critical moment in the invasion. Miraborg's sacrifice bought the Inner Sphere a year's lull in hostilities, time that proved decisive in organizing the defense that would ultimately stop the Clan advance at Tukayyid. Both the KungsArmé and the Clans honored her in their own ways: the Remembrance was amended with a passage in her memory, a new class of carrier DropShip was renamed in her honor, and the Tyra Miraborg Memorial Academy was later founded on Gunzburg to train the next generation of Rasalhague aerospace pilots.

In the years following the Clan Invasion, Wakazashi introduced the SL-17R, a modernization replacing the original single heat sinks with double-strength units that substantially improved sustained fire tolerance. Chatham production shifted toward the SL-17R as the standard Combine configuration, with the Ramora facility adding its own SL-17R line during the Jihad. As the Word of Blake's war reshaped the Inner Sphere, Wakazashi introduced the substantially redesigned SL-18, fitted with a lighter powerplant and updated weapons suite suited to that conflict's demands. A parallel experimental program produced a single prototype exploring oversized ballistic integration, an impressive technical demonstration that proved impractical for mass production.
AFShilone_SL17BATLCOS.deployment: The base SL-17 serves across every faction that operates the Shilone. In Combine service it remains the primary configuration in garrison and second-line units that have not yet received the SL-17R upgrade. Outworlds Alliance forces flying Shilones manufactured by the United Outworlders Corporation on Ramora operated almost exclusively in the base configuration during the Succession Wars. The Taurian Concordat receives the SL-17 through licensed facilities on Pinard, while the Marian Hegemony fields examples sourced from Hadrian Mechanized Industries on Pompey, where production began during the Jihad.

BMArcher_ARCB4t3.overview: One of the most iconic BattleMechs is the Archer, with its low-slung torso, enormous fists, and missile-bay covers. The Archer was first manufactured in 2474 for heavy-hitting, long-range brawling, and fire-support.
BMArcher_ARCB4t3.capabilities: Two enormous missile launchers with tons of ammo power the Archer. The missiles were formidable, but their short-range inaccuracy required four medium lasers, two rear-facing and one in each arm. Enlarged hand actuators allow the design to undertake severe physical attacks and transport captured supplies during raids. The cockpit of the Archer is situated beneath the center midsection, giving the pilot a unique battlefield view. The torso armor belt above the cockpit protects the gyro and engine from the superior armor. Many pilots initially entered battle with their missile bays locked to hide the 'Mech's real capabilities, leading some to believe it was a close-combat design. As the Archer became famous, this pretext became meaningless. Archer pilots rarely learn new skills, but this hasn't tarnished the 'Mech's reputation.
BMArcher_ARCB4t3.history: The design was constructed at the request of Terran Hegemony's HAF for a new "heavy fire support BattleMech" and took nearly nine years to complete. This owed in part to the design team, which included former HAF MechWarriors, field technicians, and general officer advisors, and the company's engineer team, led by Supervising Engineer Linn Tommi, disagreeing over theoretical and practical concerns. The intricate engineering proposal presented to the HAF includes complicated, difficult-to-repair stabilizing technology and powerful, computer-slaved sensors designed to make the Archer the most accurate BattleMech in existence. However, the final prototype abandoned these criteria in favor of a sturdier, blockier, and more heavily armored frame that is still in use today. It was so effective that it remained the Hegemony standard for more than a decade and a half, until technological developments allowed Earthwerks to produce a more efficient variant. The Archer, which debuted in 2474, quickly became one of the most well-known and commonly deployed BattleMechs. The Archer was a contemporary of 'Mechs such as the Thunderbolt and the Banshee, and its primary job was fire support, though early in its combat career it was regarded an attack 'Mech capable of long-range brawling, and it was deployed in a variety of different duties. More than 100,000 Archers were built between its introduction and the outbreak of the First Succession War, with tens of thousands of variation types produced over the centuries. Though many were destroyed or deconstructed for spare components, they remained a common sight in the Great House troops, with six distinct manufacturers creating new Archers throughout the Succession Wars. The retrieval of the Helm Memory Core had a significant impact on the creation of the Archer. New variations were created that used rediscovered lostech, giving the venerable 'Mech a few new tricks to surprise its opponents. By the time of the Clan Invasion, most of the major manufacturers had switched over to building these new variants for the Free Worlds League, Federated Commonwealth, Free Rasalhague Republic, and Wolf's Dragoons; only Vandenberg Mechanized Industries continued to build original ARC-2R Archers for the Taurian Concordat. As technology advanced, newer, more advanced models of the Archer were produced.
BMArcher_ARCB4t3.deployment: The Archer uses two Doombud LRM-20 missile launchers with four tons of ammo for two minutes of continuous fire. Side torsos shared ammo. Some Archer drivers closed their missile bay doors to confuse the adversary while the design was new, however this ploy no longer works. Archer carries four Diverse Optics Type 18 midrange lasers for close combat. Each arm has a laser, and the other two are positioned in a central turret above the cockpit, allowing them to attack targets behind the 'Mech. The Archer's large battlefists help it fight close-quarters and steal supplies during raids. The Archer cruised at 44.1 km/h and carried thirteen tons of armor. With only 10 heat sinks, an Archer firing both LRM launchers and lasers would quickly overheat. The Archer's popularity meant that most adversary pilots knew how to use it to their advantage. The Archer's cockpit, beneath the central torso, was its most distinctive feature. The Gyro and engine were protected by the torso armor belt, but this placement gave the MechWarrior a unique battlefield perspective.

BMAtlas_AS7W2.overview: "A 'Mech as powerful as possible, as impenetrable as possible, and as ugly and foreboding as conceivable, so that fear itself will be our ally.?-Aleksandr Kerensky
BMAtlas_AS7W2.capabilities: The Atlas is probably the best-known BattleMech to ever set foot on the modern battlefield. Designed with specifications from Aleksandr Kerensky himself in 2755 in the midst of the Cameron Edicts, the Atlas was originally intended to ensure SLDF superiority over the Star League member states. Carrying the largest LRM launcher, the largest autocannon, and the largest SRM launcher possible, the Atlas can deal frightening amounts of damage in short amounts of time. Often used as a command vehicle, the Atlas mounts an advanced antenna and communications array, allowing it to engage in surface-to-space communications in real time. The massive 19-ton hide of armor that protects the Atlas makes it a difficult foe to take down. Indeed, most MechWarriors choose to fall back rather than face one head-on, as its lumbering gait means it can rarely catch up to other 'Mechs that choose to flee it. A full year of development went into crafting the famous "Death's Head" of the 'Mech to achieve the perfect ratio of functionality and fear. The head is also quite roomy and allows a small satellite dish to be mounted for surface-to-space communications. During combat the pilot can easily fold up the dish and store it within a protective portion of the head.
BMAtlas_AS7W2.history: Though the inexorable arming of the Great Houses continued, the Atlas proved itself to be everything General Kerensky requested. With the largest amount of armor of nearly any 'Mech, crippling firepower, and the foreboding skull-shaped "Death's Head" cockpit/head assembly, the Atlas lived up to its reputation. The mere sight of an Atlas had been known to make even a veteran MechWarrior break out in a cold sweat, and theoretically a single Atlas can take on and wipe out an entire battalion of Stingers in exchange for minor armor loss. The Atlas' first combat trials came during the Amaris Civil War, where it served an instrumental role as a powerful command vehicle. Though General Kerensky is well-known for being the one who kicked down the palace doors of the Usurper in his Orion, it was his close friend Aaron DeChavilier who, in his Atlas, weathered the storm of enemy fire and breached the protective wall surrounding the complex. After this conflict it was therefore with little surprise that the General wished for all of these 'Mechs to accompany him on Operation Exodus, but ironically of those MechWarriors who refused his summons fully two-thirds were Atlas pilots. These units were spread among the Successor States and Atlas factories on Al Na'ir, Hesperus II and Quentin would continue production of the 'Mech through the Succession Wars. Most commanders were loath to tamper too much with such a successful 'Mech, but the recovery of the Helm Memory Core resulted in a number of ancient designs being updated with lostech, and the Atlas was no exception. The new AS7-K model was released in 3049, just in time to fight off the Clan Invasion. The Federated Commonwealth also briefly began production of their own model, the AS7-S, although following the civil war that line was discontinued and further variants have been introduced by the Lyran Alliance and Draconis Combine. Despite its age, well into the end of the thirty-first century there were no plans to replace the Atlas, and even the most cutting-edge designs will stop and pause when faced with the prospect of an Atlas bearing down on them.
BMAtlas_AS7W2.deployment: The Atlas is armed with a multitude of weapons for both long and short range combat, all designed specifically to be as visible as possible so as to strike fear in the hearts of its enemies. For long ranges, the 'Mech carries a FarFire Maxi-Rack LRM-20 in the left torso that allows it to both fire directly at an enemy target at long range, and to give indirect fire support when needed. Unable to fit a full twenty-tube system on the 'Mech, the FarFire instead launches the missiles in waves of five over the course of ten seconds and carries two tons of reloads for twelve such salvos. For close range combat the 'Mech is armed with a Defiance 'Mech Hunter Autocannon/20 in the right torso with two tons of ammo. Although lacking a cooling jacket and liable to overheat, the massive autocannon gives the Atlas the firepower to take on an entire 'Mech company. To back up the AC/20 the Atlas carries four Defiance B3M Medium Lasers, one in each arm and two mounted in the rear center torso, and a TharHes Maxi SRM-6 launcher with one ton of missiles in the right torso (the aperture between the SRM and LRM launchers is not another weapon but an omnicoupling for power and coolant cable connection). Furthermore the Atlas is equipped with hand actuators which, combined with its sheer weight and power, makes it a potent hand-to-hand fighter. Accounts of Atlases actually picking up medium-weight 'Mechs and throwing them around like toys makes for suitable horror stories and further enhances the aura of the 'Mech.

BMAwesome_AWS8WB.overview: The Awesome was designed in 2665 for the Star League by the Technicron Conglomorate and was based on the aging STR-2C Striker. While not as fast as its forefather, the Awesome is a strong assault 'Mech.
BMAwesome_AWS8WB.capabilities: The Awesome's abilities are nearly entirely dependent on its particle projection cannons. The AWS can withstand a severe and consistent onslaught from its weaponry thanks to several heat sinks. With one and a half tons more armor than the Striker, the AWS is more protected than even the BattleMaster. The Awesome, like any other BattleMech, has weaknesses. While it is lethal at range, it is less effective in close-quarters combat since its PPCs have a tougher time connecting with the victim. In that case, it just possesses a light weapon and a left fist to fall back on. Because of its limited mobility, it is vulnerable to flanking attacks from speedier opponents seeking to get past the PPCs. While they face arguably of the heaviest rear armor found on any BattleMech, the Awesome's lack of rear facing armaments or a weapon mount on its left arm has offered numerous MechWarriors a fighting chance. Formations of Awesomes (or even just a few) are incredibly effective and tough to stop or defeat when correctly placed by commanders who are knowledgeable of the AWS's limitations.
BMAwesome_AWS8WB.history: Awesomes can be found in every military House.?Because the Free Worlds League has the last remaining manufacturing factories capable of generating the Awesome, it also has the most Awesomes of any of the Great Houses. Opinions on the 'Mech vary greatly within the League. Many people laud its powers, while others believe that its limited mobility is too high a price to pay for what it can do. Similar sentiments exist in the other Houses, but none of them can debate the issue beyond academics. Few commanders would turn down the opportunity to acquire an Awesome for their army. The Awesome is typically used to assault a fixed position or to breach the enemy's line of defense. They are also in demand for defensive operations. MechWarriors piloting the Awesome can expect to be involved in heavy battle and to be charged with obtaining or guarding the most crucial objectives from the adversary.
BMAwesome_AWS8WB.deployment: The Awesome has a limited, but effective, armament consisting of three Kreuss PPCs, one mounted in its right arm and two split between the left and right torsos. These give it an immense amount of damage potential at ranges exceeding five hundred meters, enough to destroy some 'Mechs with a single salvo, although at point-blank range they are less useful. For close combat the 'Mech mounts in its head a Diverse Optics Type 10 Small Laser while its left arm ends in a battlefist sufficient for hand-to-hand fighting.

BMBlackKnight_BL18KNTW.overview:
The Black Knight was introduced in 2578 by Kong Interstellar Corporation as both a front-line combatant and a company- and battalion-level command BattleMech for the Star League Defense Force. Equipped with an advanced communications suite capable of coordinating an entire company of 'Mechs, linking command frequencies across a regiment, and connecting with orbital support satellites, the Black Knight quickly established itself as one of the premier heavy BattleMechs of the Star League era. Built with heavy armor and an all-energy weapons array, the design earned a fearsome reputation that endured across centuries of warfare.

Though the Succession Wars drastically reduced the Black Knight's numbers, the design survived through ComStar stockpiles, field modifications, and the determination of its operators. Production eventually resumed in the 3060s through Robinson Standard BattleWorks and Kong Interstellar's rebuilt facilities, and a succession of increasingly advanced variants has kept the Black Knight relevant on the modern battlefield.
BMBlackKnight_BL18KNTW.capabilities:
The Black Knight is an all-energy-weapon platform anchored by a Magna Hellstar II PPC, supported by two large lasers, four medium lasers, and a small laser integrated directly into its Beagle Active Probe. This sensor-weapon linkage allows the scanner to piggyback low-power laser pulses through interfering objects, providing detailed analysis of nearby targets that few other designs can match. Thirteen tons of Valiant Lamellor armor on a Technicron endo steel frame delivers exceptional survivability for a seventy-five-ton chassis, while the standard Vlar 300 engine provides a reliable top speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour without the fragility of an extralight powerplant.

The design's primary weakness has always been heat management. Despite mounting twenty single heat sinks, the sheer volume of energy weapons generates heat faster than the cooling system can dissipate it during sustained engagements. MechWarriors must exercise strict fire discipline, selecting weapon groups appropriate to the engagement range rather than attempting full alpha strikes. The original Black Knight's reputation in the Third Heavy Assault Regiment was that of a 'Mech which had to be literally dismembered to stop, and in one-on-one engagements between equally skilled pilots, conventional wisdom holds that the Black Knight will always triumph.
BMBlackKnight_BL18KNTW.history:
The Black Knight debuted during the Reunification War in 2578 when Kong Interstellar Corporation's Third Heavy Assault Regiment (the Pythons) fielded the new design against the Taurian Concordat on Ridgebrook. Company commanders quickly discovered that the sophisticated electronics package made the Black Knight an outstanding command platform, and following its successful combat debut, the SLDF's First Corps and eventually the entire Defense Force adopted the design. By the height of the Star League, the Black Knight was a ubiquitous presence in SLDF formations, with Royal regiments fielding the advanced BL-6b-KNT variant equipped with double heat sinks and upgraded weaponry.

The collapse of the Star League and the devastation of the First Succession War proved catastrophic for Black Knight production. Kong Interstellar's orbital factories above Connaught were destroyed in 2802, and while the company managed to restart production in 2809 with the downgraded BL-7-KNT (replacing the endo steel chassis and advanced electronics with cruder but manufacturable alternatives) a Capellan Confederation raid permanently destroyed the line in 2820. Kong was reduced to producing spare parts and performing maintenance work, and the Black Knight's numbers slowly dwindled across the Inner Sphere as attrition and jury-rigged repairs took their toll.

During the Succession Wars, the remaining Black Knights were concentrated primarily in the Federated Suns and Free Worlds League, while the Capellan Confederation possessed none. ComStar maintained stockpiles of Star League-era machines, which proved invaluable when the Com Guards adopted the Black Knight as a command unit for Level II and Level III formations. Curiously, the handful of Black Knights provided to the Draconis Combine through Operation ROSEBUD was apparently the result of a clerical error. The Clans also maintained the design, though by the time of the Clan Invasion it had been relegated to solahma units.

The Battle of Tukayyid in 3052 marked the Black Knight's dramatic return to prominence. ComStar engineers developed the BL-9-KNT Clanbuster refit specifically for the engagement, equipping it with an XL engine, upgraded weapons, and a distinctive sword-like hatchet designed to exploit the Clans' disdain for physical combat. These machines proved remarkably effective in the close-quarters fighting of the Racice River Delta against Clan Smoke Jaguar and at Devil's Bath against the Steel Vipers, where the improved short-range firepower and melee capability caught Clan warriors off guard.

Robinson Standard BattleWorks secured a manufacturing license from Kong Interstellar in 3063, producing the technologically advanced BL-12-KNT with extended-range weapons and a targeting computer. Two years later, Kong itself rebuilt its Connaught plant and resumed Black Knight production. Through the Jihad and into the Dark Age, RSB released a succession of increasingly sophisticated BLK-NT variants incorporating Clan-specification weaponry, endo-composite structures, and advanced electronic warfare suites. When the Republic of the Sphere collapsed, Kong received the BLK-NT plans through a reciprocal licensing agreement with RSB and developed its own variant, the BL-18-KNT, updating the classic design with Clan weapons and a targeting computer. The Black Knight has thus endured across nearly six centuries of continuous service, proof of the fundamental soundness of Kong Interstellar's original design.
BMBlackKnight_BL18KNTW.deployment: Produced by Kong Interstellar for the Republic of the Sphere, this variant emerged from a reciprocal licensing agreement through which Kong received Robinson Standard BattleWorks' BLK-NT series plans. Rather than simply manufacturing the Robinson design, Kong applied the new technology to their own classic Black Knight lineage. The variant mounts an endo-composite frame and Vlar 300 light engine, armed with a full suite of Clan-specification weapons including an ER PPC, two ER large lasers, four ER medium lasers, and a Clan small pulse laser for anti-infantry work. Twenty Clan-built double heat sinks provide substantially improved cooling, and an Inner Sphere targeting computer ties the entire weapons array together for devastating accuracy.

BMBombardier_BMB10DBATLCOS.overview:
The Bombardier was proposed to the Star League in 2735 by Wakazashi Enterprises as a specialized sixty-five-ton fire support BattleMech designed to replace less-mobile artillery vehicles that might fall behind in an advance or be destroyed by counterbattery fire. The design used specialized missile racks capable of carrying diverse types of advanced munitions, filling the role of a mobile artillery platform that could keep pace with advancing BattleMech formations while delivering devastating long-range firepower.

The Bombardier's reputation has fluctuated dramatically over the centuries, from a promising Star League-era fire support platform to a near-extinct relic of the Succession Wars. Multiple manufacturers across the Inner Sphere and Periphery have since revived the design, and the Bombardier's long-range fire support role has proven as relevant in the post-Jihad era as it was during the Star League.
BMBombardier_BMB10DBATLCOS.capabilities:
The original BMB-12D mounts a pair of Delphinius-20 LRM launchers as its primary armament, weapons specifically designed to handle unique Star League-era ammunition types such as Swarm and Thunder missiles. A VOX 325 XL engine provides a respectable top speed of eighty-six kilometers per hour, allowing the Bombardier to keep pace with advancing formations and reposition as needed. Choutaka Armorscale protection with CASE provides solid defensive coverage for a fire support platform, and a Buzzsaw anti-missile system offers additional protection against incoming missile fire.

The Bombardier's greatest weakness is its limited endurance. With only two tons of LRM ammunition providing a mere twelve salvos, the design cannot sustain fire in an extended engagement. An Arrowlite-4 SRM launcher in the right arm provides some defense against units that close inside the LRMs' minimum effective range, but it carries only a single ton of ammunition and is insufficient to repel a determined assault. Unlike comparable fire support designs such as the Archer, the Bombardier carries no energy weapons to fall back on once its missile stores are depleted, leaving MechWarriors with a well-armored but toothless machine once the ammunition runs dry.
BMBombardier_BMB10DBATLCOS.history:
The Bombardier's history is one of promise unfulfilled and unlikely resurrection. Proposed in 2735 by Wakazashi Enterprises on Al Na'ir, the design was conceived as a BattleMech replacement for conventional artillery vehicles, offering superior mobility and survivability while maintaining devastating long-range firepower. The Star League Defense Force embraced the concept, and the Bombardier performed admirably in exercises and limited deployments during the final decades of the Star League era. By the time of the Amaris Civil War and the subsequent Exodus, more than eight hundred Bombardiers were distributed across SLDF formations.

The Succession Wars proved catastrophic for the design. The specialized Bombardier Artillery Missiles that gave the chassis its name were consumed at staggering rates during the First Succession War, with many garrison worlds exhausting their entire stockpiles within days of sustained combat. Forced into close-support roles for which it was never designed, the Bombardier suffered the highest battlefield loss rate of any BattleMech type. Wakazashi's primary factory on Al Na'ir was destroyed during the First Succession War, and the company, increasingly focused on aerospace production, saw no reason to rebuild capacity for a design with such a poor battlefield reputation.

Earthwerks Incorporated on Calloway VI obtained a license from Wakazashi to produce spare parts and began refitting surviving Bombardiers into the simplified BMB-10D configuration during the late Succession Wars. These refits kept the design alive in small numbers, though most were consigned to militia garrisons or reserve formations in the Free Worlds League and Draconis Combine. The Federated Commonwealth assigned its Bombardiers to training cadres where their limited ammunition was a manageable constraint rather than a battlefield liability. The Delphinius LRM-20 launchers salvaged from surviving 12Ds found second lives as replacement components for Archers, Apollos, and Catapults, meaning that a working Bombardier in the field was often a sign that the unit fielding it was on its last legs.

The Bombardier's most dramatic chapter began with the Clan Invasion's aftermath. The Outworlds Alliance, long dismissed as a minor Periphery power, forged a partnership with Clan Snow Raven that transformed the Alliance's industrial base. A massive factory complex, Clan enclave, and DropShip repair facility appeared on Mitchella, and the United Outworlders Corporation began producing both new BMB-12Ds and the radically upgraded BMB-05A. When Alliance Grenadiers fielded these new Bombardiers during a raid against Enif, Combine intelligence agents took immediate notice. The once-timid Alliance was mass-producing effective fire support 'Mechs, prompting Wakazashi to begin refitting older Bombardier frames into the MML-equipped BMB-14K at facilities on Dover and New Samarkand.

ComStar's secret development of the BMB-14C added another thread to the design's revival, though the Word of Blake schism and subsequent Jihad left the fate of these machines uncertain. By the early thirty-second century, the Bombardier had gone from a design on the verge of extinction to one actively produced and refitted by multiple factions, its long-range fire support role proving as relevant in the post-Jihad era as it had been during the Star League.
BMBombardier_BMB10DBATLCOS.deployment: This variant is a Succession Wars-era refit performed by Earthwerks Incorporated on their Calloway VI facility after Wakazashi licensed them to produce replacement parts. The advanced Delphinius and Arrowlite launchers were replaced with lower-technology Doombud LRM-20 and Hovertech SRM-4 models, and the Buzzsaw anti-missile system gave way to a Voelkers 200 machine gun. Most significantly, the VOX 325 XL engine was swapped for a smaller Magna 260, reducing top speed to just sixty-four kilometers per hour. The loss of CASE protection for the ammunition stores makes the 10D more vulnerable to catastrophic ammunition explosions, though armor coverage remains unchanged. Communications and targeting systems were likewise downgraded to a Neil 5000 and RCA Instatrac Mark XII respectively. The 10D saw service primarily with Free Worlds League and Draconis Combine militia units, while the Federated Commonwealth relegated theirs to training academies where ammunition shortages were less problematic.

BMClint_CLNT23WL2.overview: The Clint was primarily designed as a cheap recon unit, with the capabilities of a well-armed, low-end medium weight 'Mech, and in this regard it served well.
BMClint_CLNT23WL2.capabilities: With a top speed of 97.2 km/h and a jumping capability of 180 meters, the Clint can easily keep up with other recon elements and maneuver through mountainous or urban terrain. Its Sloan 220 Lockover T&T system in particular shines, as it is simple to use and provides the pilot with excellent battlefield data. Although the 'Mech has limited ammunition reserves for its autocannon, the Sloane 220 ensures that whatever the Clint shoots at, it hits.
BMClint_CLNT23WL2.history: The Clint was built in 2607 as a direct result of the Star League Armaments Act, a law intended to provide frontier areas with cutting-edge warfare technology. However, Andoran Industries Ltd., a tiny BattleMech firm based on Bell, won the project by undercutting its competitors with cost-cutting design features. The Clint was not only made with substandard parts that rarely lasted a year, but it also employed very few standard components; modular pieces that could be easily transferred between many different 'Mechs could not be used in the Clint without extensive modification. The machine became a technician's nightmare, requiring more time to fix than comparable 'Mechs and allowing Andoran to recoup the Clint's low purchase price with a costly service contract. Before the Star League crumbled, over 300 Clints were created, and Andoran's factories were destroyed during conflict between the Federated Suns and the Capellan Confederation. House Davion and House Liao seized the majority of the remaining Clints and dispatched them to isolated regions inside their realms for defense purposes, however the Capellans retained several of the 'Mechs in front-line troops. Nonetheless, the explosion of the Bell facility destroyed not only the original Clint blueprints, effectively terminating new unit and spare part production, but also records of the exact number of Clints made and variants created. Clints could therefore be found across the Inner Sphere throughout the Succession Wars, proving rather popular in the Periphery, although the origins of many of these machines, and whether their different loadouts were official manufacture modifications or simple field-refits, remained unknown. Furthermore, the Clint's non-standard components quickly rose in price - the gyro, in instance, became worth its weight in gold - and many were simply stripped for parts to fix damaged machines. Despite the design's inherent maintenance challenges, an estimated 200 Clints remained in service until the Clan Invasion, largely in the hands of the Capellans or scattered throughout the Suns' border regions. The Confederation also created the 3U model, which the Federated Commonwealth swiftly adopted after the Bell Refit Yards were erected on the ruins of the original factory complex. The plans for the design finally made their way to Defiance Industries of Furillo, which began constructing new Clints for the first time in millennia in 3055.
BMClint_CLNT23WL2.deployment: The Clint was initially intended to carry an Armstrong Buster AC/10, but due to issues with the 'Mech's stress limits, the autocannon was lowered to an Armstrong J11 AC/5 with one ton of ammunition. The Clint carries two Martell midrange lasers as backup weaponry. When combined with the Clint's above-average mobility for its size, this well-balanced arsenal of weapons makes the Clint a very effective multirole BattleMech.

BMCrab_CRB20R.overview: Designed in 2719 during the last days of the Star League, the Crab was built as a medium-weight raider and guerrilla fighter for the Star League Defense Force.
BMCrab_CRB20R.capabilities: Although lacking hand actuators or jump jets, it possessed good overland speed and its all-energy weapons payload was suitable for long-range missions without the prospect for resupply. The Crab also boasted a highly advanced communications system, the Dalban Series K, and was built mostly with proven parts easy to maintain. The term "Crab walk" soon became synonymous with easy duty, since technicians spent less than half the time maintaining the Crab than with other 'Mechs of the same weight class.
BMCrab_CRB20R.history: Less than a thousand Crabs had been produced when the Succession Wars began. So popular was the Crab that many believed it was likely to become the standard medium 'Mech of the SLDF. Unfortunately the Amaris Civil War and the dissolution of the Star League put an end to any future plans for the Crab. Cosara Weaponries' Crab factory on Northwind was practically destroyed in 2786, one of many strategic targets attacked in the opening salvos of the First Succession War. Although dedicated technicians were able to keep portions of the assembly line open, producing what spare parts they still could to rebuild damaged Crabs, the technology used for both the original's advanced armor plating and communications system became lost. Designated as CRB-20 models, these Crabs were only slightly inferior to the original: with the destruction of the military infrastructure necessary for the Dalban Series K's more advanced functions to work, its replacement by lesser systems ironically became less of an issue. By the end of the Fourth Succession War a hundred or so Crabs were still active in the Inner Sphere and all were CRB-20s. Unbeknownst to many, ComStar had secreted away massive stockpiles of Star League technology and 'Mechs, including the Crab. When it came time to form their own military original CRB-27 Crabs were used to outfit the Com Guards, while at the same time gifting downgraded CRB-20s to the Draconis Combine during the War of 3039 as part of Operation Rosebud. Concurrently the discovery of the Helm Memory Core allowed the refit line on Northwind to start upgrading the remaining downgraded Crabs to their original specification. Unknown to anyone in the Inner Sphere was the continued existence of the Crab in the arsenal of the Clans, although by the time of the Clan Invasion these had been relegated to second-line and garrison units. Eventually Cosara Weaponries was able to restart production of the original Crab in the 3050s and brand-new variants began turning up. Among these were new CRB-30s built by ComStar (later acquired by the Word of Blake) which made use of new C3 technology; it was also rumored ComStar sold these models to the rump Free Rasalhague Republic. During the Jihad the Word of Blake managed to capture the Northwind factory and begin producing their own radical variant known as the CRB-45.
BMCrab_CRB20R.deployment: The CRB-20 is a downgrade of the CRB-27 Crab, first sighted in 2810. The only major modifications to the design was the use of standard armor which reduced the overall protection on the Crab and the replacement of its electronic systems with more reliable off-the-shelf models. When ComStar gifted their Crabs to the Draconis Combine they replaced the original components with a Garret T-11b communications system and a Garret D2j targeting and tracking system.

BMCyclops_CPANVIL.overview: The Cyclops began production in 2710 as an assault BattleMech and headquarters unit for Star League Defense Force field commanders.
BMCyclops_CPANVIL.capabilities: A decent mix of weapons provided the Cyclops with both long- and short-range firepower and a sizable engine to keep up with mobile operations. But the centerpiece of the Cyclops is its sophisticated holographic battle computer, the Tacticon B-2000. When combined with the Olmstead 840 tight beam comm suite with SatNav module, the Cyclops can effectively command a brigade across the surface of an entire world. Unfortunately the Cyclops is poorly protected relative to other assault 'Mechs with only ten tons of armor, and while its normal load of twelve heat sinks allows it to stay cool in most cases, they can prove to be inadequate in especially heavy situations.
BMCyclops_CPANVIL.history: Unfortunately the Cyclops did not fare so well with the onset of the Amaris Civil War when the Rim Worlds Republic Military destroyed its primary factory on Caph in 2774. Spare parts for the machine quickly began to dry up, until by the end of the Succession Wars less than ten percent still had a working B-2000 computer. Lacking the critical part of being a command vehicle many Cyclopses were pressed into an assault role. Acting as the bodyguard or decoy for the real commanding officer, they proved to be swift if mediocre combat machines. As most enemies know about the vulnerable head and automatically target it in combat, many Cyclops pilots also began adding false head protectors to defend against impacts. A study by the NAIS after the Fourth Succession War would eventually find that these caused more harm than good by restricting vision and increasing shrapnel, ending the practice altogether. The rediscovery of the Helm Memory Core kick-started a number of attempts to replicate the B-2000 computer, however there were no successful attempts prior to the Clan Invasion. Also, the invention of the C3 Computer with its emphasis on small-scale networking, and a switch in doctrine to using DropShips as command posts, saw the Cyclops' command role decline. However Grumium Creations was eventually able to restart production of new variants of the 'Mech, and where it has participated a Cyclops with a working B-2000 has had noticeable effects. For this reason Cyclops 'Mechs with a working battle computer were reserved for high-ranking officers.
BMCyclops_CPANVIL.deployment: The Cyclops carries an arsenal built to handle almost any situation. For long-range combat and indirect fire, the 'Mech carries a Delta Dart LRM-10 missile launcher in the left torso along with one ton of reloads. For closer ranges the 'Mech has a variety of weapons. A Zeus-36, Mark III Autocannon/20 mounted in the right torso keeps all but the heaviest 'Mechs at a respectable distance and is fed by four tons of ammo split between both sides of the torso. The autocannon is backed up by two Diverse Optics Type 20 Medium Lasers, one in either arm, and a Hovertec Quad SRM-4 with one ton of reloads in the center torso.

BMEnforcer_ENF4K.overview: Since it first walked off of the production line, the Enforcer has been the iconic medium-weight workhorse of the Federated Suns' Succession Wars era military.
BMEnforcer_ENF4K.capabilities: The Enforcer fulfilled the roles of a mobile barrage vehicle, laying down an intense hail of fire as a prelude to an offensive or to blunt an enemy's attack, and as a trooper 'Mech, using its thick frontal armor and good jumping distance of one hundred and twenty meters to effectively brawl with the enemy despite lacking hand actuators. The sturdy and inexpensive design's mobility also made it an ideal city fighter, especially when sniping the enemy during hit-and-run attacks. One of the design's problems was that, with most of its nine tons of armor concentrated forward, the amount of protection in its rear torso is less than on some light 'Mechs. The Enforcer's biggest flaw though was its limited ammunition stores, though when possible a truck-and-crane reloading system is used during less-mobile battles. Attempts were made to replace the small laser with another ton of ammunition, however there were complicated linkage problems in getting the ammo from the left torso to the right arm, increasing the rate of jamming or reducing the rate of fire to unacceptable levels. What's more the rounds had to be routed along the 'Mechs back where its armor was weakest.
BMEnforcer_ENF4K.history: This is in large part due to production of the Enforcer remaining largely undisturbed throughout the Succession Wars, despite the relative lack of industrialization that has long hampered the Federated Suns. With the autocannon-obsessed Armed Forces of the Federated Suns building up its BattleMech forces upon the collapse of the Star League, the discovery on Achernar of schematics for an unbuilt autocannon-carrying Star League 'Mech was a case of perfect timing. Modifying the design by swapping two medium lasers for a single larger one, Achernar BattleMechs rushed it through development and began production in 2777.
BMEnforcer_ENF4K.deployment: The Enforcer's primary weapon is a Federated Autocannon, an excellent large-caliber model firing in bursts of ten rounds and whose cooling jacket doubles as a protective sleeve for engaging in hand-to-hand combat. While one ton of ammunition only allows for ten bursts total, the rounds are stored in an equivalent number of big clips which are easy to eject and reload. Complementing the autocannon is a ChisComp 43 Large Laser in the left arm, both giving the Enforcer respectable intermediate range firepower, while a ChisComp 32 Small Laser in the left torso provides for close range combat.

BMFirefly_FFL4ABATLCOS.overview:
Entering service in 2669, the Firefly was one of the standard light BattleMechs of the Star League Defense Force in its later years. Designed by the Coventry/Earthwerks Combine on Terra, the thirty-ton Firefly was built not as a scout but as a light support 'Mech, its superior armor and armament allowing it to serve as the anvil against which the rest of its lance could crush enemy reconnaissance forces. The design also proved highly effective when deployed independently in urban environments, where its jump capability gave it a decisive edge against infantry and light combat vehicles.

The Firefly endured, however, among the Star League exiles who had accompanied General Kerensky on the Exodus, seeing continued production on Strana Mechty and extensive service through Operation KLONDIKE and the founding of the Clans. BMFirefly_FFL4ABATLCOS.capabilities:
Though too slow to serve as a true scout when measured against other thirty-ton designs, the Firefly compensates with impressive durability and firepower for its weight class. The base chassis mounts nearly the maximum armor protection available for a 'Mech of its tonnage, giving it a survivability advantage that few light designs can match. Four Lexington Lifters jump jets provide 120 meters of leaping capability, granting the Firefly excellent tactical mobility in broken terrain and urban landscapes despite its modest ground speed of 86 kilometers per hour.

The standard armament centers on three Martell medium lasers supplemented by a Coventry Five-Tube LRM-5 launcher, providing effective engagement capability at both close and extended ranges. Various models add small lasers, anti-missile systems, or electronic warfare equipment depending on the intended tactical role. This combination of heavy armor, respectable firepower, and jump capability makes the Firefly an effective light brawler, though its lack of speed relative to dedicated scouts means it must rely on terrain and ambush tactics rather than raw velocity to survive on the battlefield.

The Earthwerks Firefly chassis has proven remarkably adaptable across centuries of service, supporting configurations ranging from the original Star League specification with advanced technologies like XL engines and double heat sinks to the stripped-down Succession Wars variants that served Wolf's Dragoons faithfully with far simpler components.
BMFirefly_FFL4ABATLCOS.history:
The Firefly's service history spans over five centuries and encompasses some of the most critical conflicts in human history. Originally manufactured by the Coventry/Earthwerks Combine on Terra, the design entered SLDF service in 2669 and quickly established itself as a reliable light support platform. When the Star League collapsed and General Kerensky led the Exodus in 2784, significant numbers of Fireflys accompanied the departing SLDF forces, while the Combine's Terra factory was destroyed in 2779 during the opening salvos of the Succession Wars.

Among the exiles, the Firefly thrived. Strana Mechty MechWorks established new production of the FFL-3SLE variant, and the design served on both sides of the Exodus Civil War and throughout Operation KLONDIKE. Even the most degraded examples fielded by the Pentagon Powers proto-states performed creditably thanks to the inherent robustness of the Firefly's design. When the Clans eventually activated Wolf's Dragoons for their intelligence-gathering mission to the Inner Sphere, the Firefly was among the designs selected, though deliberately downgraded to Succession Wars technology levels to avoid revealing the Dragoons' true origins.

Acting as the backbone of the Dragoons' light 'Mech formations, the Firefly served with distinction through the Third and Fourth Succession Wars. Cut off from Clan Homeworld resupply, however, the Dragoons' Firefly inventory steadily dwindled over the decades. The late 3040s saw the first upgrades as the Dragoons prepared for the anticipated Clan invasion, producing the FFL-4B field modification. The design's wider distribution began when ComStar unveiled refitted FFL-4C models with their Com Guards, and the Invading Clans fielded upgraded Firefly C variants among their second-line forces.

By the time of the Word of Blake Jihad and the devastation of Outreach in 3067, fewer than half a dozen Fireflys remained in Dragoon service, though rumors persisted of advanced models produced at an unknown facility. New production of the FFL-4D was established at both Arc-Royal MechWorks and Blackwell Corporation on Outreach shortly before the Jihad consumed both worlds in conflict. The design's fortunes were finally reversed nearly a century later when Wolf's Dragoons, seeking to diversify their logistics, contracted with Ceres Metals Industries on Lockton to produce the new FFL-5A model, restoring the Firefly to prominence among the Dragoons' light combat units and making it available to other mercenary commands for the first time.
BMFirefly_FFL4ABATLCOS.deployment: The downgraded Succession Wars-era variant that accompanied Wolf's Dragoons to the Inner Sphere, this variant replaces the advanced technologies of the FFL-3A with readily available components to disguise the Dragoons' Clan origins. Mounting a standard fusion engine, single heat sinks, and standard armor, it retains a similar weapons payload to the later FFL-4B, carrying three medium lasers and four Light Martell small lasers alongside an LRM-5 launcher. Despite its technological regression, this variant served the Dragoons faithfully for decades and confounded Inner Sphere intelligence services with its resemblance to a design thought long extinct.

BMGriffin_GRF1W1.overview: Built in 2492 the Griffin was originally classified as a heavy BattleMech, filling in the weight gap between mammoth machines like the Mackie and smaller recon 'Mechs like the Wasp, and intended for close assaults
BMGriffin_GRF1W1.capabilities: The massive and efficient fusion engine of the Griffin, giving it a cruising speed of 57.1 km/h, combined with five jump jets occupying the rear torso areas for a total jumping distance of 150 meters, is what distinguishes it from other medium 'Mechs and has kept the Griffin in the game over the centuries. Unfortunately, like most other early 'Mechs, the Griffin suffers from insufficient heat capacity with only twelve heat sinks installed. The result is that Griffin pilots, lacking the ability to do both, must choose at the outset of a fight whether to engage or withdraw. Nine and a half tons of armor plating compares quite favorably to many other medium 'Mechs, although as is often the case the Griffin will find itself in combat with larger 'Mechs. For this reason, two pairs of false armor baffles were added to the 'Mech, one on its shoulders providing limited protection to the LRM launcher and cockpit, and a smaller pair on the legs protecting the knees joints.
BMGriffin_GRF1W1.history: Combining tremendous speed and firepower in one frame the Griffin briefly dominated in this role before being superseded by larger and better-equipped 'Mechs. However the Griffin was very popular among commanders and pilots alike and so Earthwerks Incorporated kept it in production, this time reclassified as a medium 'Mech and tasked with long-range fire support for medium lances. In this capacity the Griffin has excelled, combining good striking power, endurance and speed, with its only major weakness being a lack of close-range defensive weapons. During the Succession Wars the Griffin could be found in almost every unit of all the Great Houses, thanks in part to its diverse number of manufacturers. Besides being constructed from Earthwerks' factory on Keystone the Griffin was later acquired and built by Defiance Industries (Hesperus II), Kallon Industries (Talon), Brigadier Corporation (Oliver), and Norse BattleMech Works (later Victory Industries, Marduk). It was even manufactured in the Periphery by Vandenberg Mechanized Industries on Illiushin. Only the Capellan Confederation lacked a means of building the 'Mech, although they made up for it by purchasing a limited number from the Taurian Concordat. During the Fourth Succession War some of these manufacturers exchanged hands, with the Draconis Combine capturing Marduk from the Federated Suns and the Lyran Commonwealth taking Oliver from the Free Worlds League. This exchange also happened to coincide with several new variants being designed to exploit recently-recovered lostech. As such variants meant specifically for either Houses Kurita, Marik or the Federated Commonwealth found their way into the arsenals of all of them. During the Clan Invasion these manufacturers produced the new variants to meet the Clan threat while Vandenberg Industries continued to build original GRF-1N Griffins. When Vicore Industries began shopping around its "Project Phoenix" initiative, Defiance and Kallon Industries signed on to begin producing the completely redesigned GRF-6S Griffin. Victory Industries later signed up as well after the legal battle between Wolf's Dragoons and the Lyran Alliance saw the famous mercenary group selling its Light Fusion technology to both the Draconis Combine and Free Worlds League. The League designed a native update to the Griffin while ComStar had their own built as well which, ominously, soon began appearing in the ranks of the Word of Blake Militia. The Griffin would continue to remain a staple of the battlefields of the Inner Sphere during the maelstrom of the Jihad, the era of the Republic of the Sphere and the rise of the ilClan, with models still in production within the Free Worlds League and the Wolf Empire.
BMGriffin_GRF1W1.deployment: The primary weapon on the Griffin is a Fusigon PPC in the right arm. The PPC allows the Griffin to work in a long-range fire support role and is backed up by a Delta Dart LRM-10 launcher mounted in a drum over the right shoulder. The LRM launcher also gives the Griffin some indirect fire support capabilities and the two tons of reloads in the right torso allows for good endurance. The Achilles' heel of the design is its lack of short-range weapons, for when an enemy is capable of closing ranges and engaging in close quarters combat, and the fact that all of its weapons are located on the right side. The 'Mech is however equipped with two powerful battle fists for hand-to-hand combat.

BMGrizzly_W.overview:
The Grizzly is a seventy-ton heavy BattleMech developed by Clan Ghost Bear scientists during the late 29th century, entering production in 2947 at the Arcadia facility. Designed as a multi-role combatant, the Grizzly was intended to serve as a versatile heavy 'Mech capable of engaging targets across all range brackets. Unfortunately, this broad design philosophy earned it the enduring stigma of being a "jack of all trades, master of none," preventing the Grizzly from carving a dedicated niche within the Ghost Bear touman.

Persistent engineering flaws compounded its middling combat role, and Clan Ghost Bear ceased production in 3013. Despite this inauspicious early history, the Grizzly would see renewed interest and multiple production revivals centuries after its original lines went cold, proving that even a mediocre chassis can find new purpose with the right modifications.
BMGrizzly_W.capabilities:
The Grizzly rides on a Type 56-45C Modified Endo Steel chassis powered by a 280-rated RFUM fusion engine, achieving a top speed of 64 kph. Four Clan Standard 14X Series jump jets provide 120 meters of jump capability, granting the design unusual mobility for a seventy-ton 'Mech. Thirteen tons of Arcadia Compound Delta VII Standard armor offer reasonable protection, though the design's notorious armor slagging problem creates a persistent maintenance burden as damaged plating jams into joints and weapon ports during sustained combat.

The Grizzly's armament covers multiple engagement ranges. An Omega 12-coil Gauss rifle serves as the primary long-range weapon, delivering devastating kinetic strikes without generating waste heat. A Type X "Short Bow" LRM-10 launcher supplements this reach with indirect fire capability. At closer ranges, a trio of pulse lasers (a Kolibri Delta Series Large Pulse Laser, a matching Medium Pulse Laser, and a Chi Series Small Pulse Laser) provide accurate fire against maneuvering targets.

While this loadout is competent at every range, it lacks the focused firepower to dominate any single engagement bracket. The Grizzly cannot match dedicated fire support designs at distance nor overwhelm close-combat specialists in a brawl, reinforcing its reputation as a capable but unremarkable generalist.
BMGrizzly_W.history:
The Grizzly's origins trace to the late 29th century, when Clan Ghost Bear scientists sought to develop a versatile heavy BattleMech for garrison duty. Production began in 2947 at the Arcadia BattleMech Plant CM-T02 on Arcadia, but the design struggled to find advocates within the competitive trial-based culture of the Clans. Sharing design concepts with the more prevalent Vulture and Gladiator OmniMechs, the Grizzly was unfavorably compared to both, lacking the specialization that Clan warriors valued. Engineering deficiencies (particularly the armor slagging issue and difficult-to-service actuators) further eroded confidence in the platform.

By 3013, Clan Ghost Bear officially ceased production of the Grizzly, with the remaining 'Mechs scattered among Provisional Garrison Clusters. For decades, the design languished in obscurity, typically assigned to green warriors or used as training platforms. The Grizzly seemed destined for quiet obsolescence.

The Combine-Ghost Bear War of 3062-3063 unexpectedly revived the Grizzly's fortunes. During fierce urban combat on Last Frontier, a custom Grizzly configuration proved remarkably effective as an urban defender, demonstrating that the chassis still had untapped potential when properly armed. Impressed by this success, Clan Ghost Bear ordered the custom loadout standardized as the Grizzly 2, with Bergan Industries at Jarett beginning factory production alongside widespread field refits of existing airframes. The variant's effectiveness against battle armor and infantry made it particularly valuable during the Jihad, though the destruction of the Jarett facility in 3078 by Mostrand separatists ended formal factory production.

The Grizzly's story took another dramatic turn in the early 32nd century. Jötunn BattleWorx, a newcomer to BattleMech manufacturing founded in 3132 on Goito within the Rasalhague Dominion, selected the Grizzly as the testbed for their pioneering reinforced chassis technology. Flush with resources from Gray Monday appropriations and Bear-Krona partnerships, Jötunn acquired an old Grizzly and spent four years testing endless weapon and structural permutations before the Grizzly 3 walked off their first production line in 3138. Though the initial production run was described as highly compromised, the lessons learned proved invaluable, directly informing the subsequent development of Jötunn's Rime Otter OmniMech and Mastodon assault OmniMech.

Through its turbulent history, the Grizzly has changed hands multiple times at the factory level. The original Arcadia facility passed from Clan Ghost Bear to Clan Blood Spirit during the Jihad era, and subsequently fell under Clan Star Adder's control, though production never resumed there. The broader political shifts that saw Jarett transition from Draconis Combine control to Clan Ghost Bear and eventually to the Rasalhague Dominion mirrored the Grizzly's own evolution from a pure Clan design to a product of the Inner Sphere-Clan hybrid culture of the Dominion.
BMGrizzly_W.deployment: The base Grizzly represents the original production model that rolled off the Arcadia assembly lines beginning in 2947. Armed with a balanced mix of Gauss rifle, missiles, and pulse lasers, it was designed as a versatile garrison combatant capable of engaging threats at any range. Despite its competent armament, the combination of persistent engineering flaws and lack of tactical focus saw the design gradually marginalized within the Ghost Bear touman. Production ceased in 3013, and surviving examples were shuffled to increasingly junior formations, where they served as training platforms and rear-echelon garrison units for decades. With word of atrocities occurring in the Rasalhague Republic during the Jihad, however, the Bear Touman began re-examining this out-of-production design for immediate manufacture to quickly bolster materiel for anticipated operations.

BMHammerhead_2Unofficial.overview: The Hammerhead is a 45-ton medium Clan BattleMech introduced in 3146 by Clan Sea Fox. Designed as an aggressive shock trooper, the Hammerhead represents an unconventional approach to Clan medium 'Mech design, trading the speed and firepower typical of its weight class for exceptional resilience. Loosely resembling its aquatic namesake, the 'Mech quickly became a signature element of the Sea Fox touman and achieved strong export sales across multiple Clans. Its emphasis on pilot survivability over raw lethality made it particularly valued for training formations and garrison assignments, cementing its place as one of the most commercially successful Clan designs of the ilClan era.
BMHammerhead_2Unofficial.capabilities:
The Hammerhead was conceived around an unconventional philosophy for Clan warfare: keeping inexperienced MechWarriors alive long enough to learn from their mistakes. Its defining characteristic is fifteen tons of Double-Forged ZX20 hardened armor, granting protection equivalent to many assault-class 'Mechs despite its medium weight classification. This exceptional protection is complemented by leg-mounted actuator enhancement systems that counteract the hardened armor's inherent clumsiness, making the 'Mech remarkably difficult to knock down. Built on an SFAM endo steel skeleton and powered by a Firebox 270 XL engine, the Hammerhead achieves a respectable top speed of 86.4 km/h, though the weight of its hardened plating limits its effective running speed compared to similarly sized designs.

The armament is deliberately modest. A Series 44h large pulse laser serves as the primary weapon, offering accurate fire at medium ranges, while a Series 2b extended-range medium laser and a Type VI Streak SRM-6 provide additional close-range punch. This loadout reflects the Hammerhead's intended role as a brawler rather than a stand-off combatant. The design trades overwhelming firepower for the ability to absorb tremendous punishment, wading through enemy formations and engaging heavier opponents at ranges where its toughness matters most. The 'Mech's Battlefist-equipped arms further enhance its effectiveness in close combat, though pilots must be mindful that the hardened armor's weight penalty leaves the Hammerhead vulnerable to faster opponents that can dictate engagement range.
BMHammerhead_2Unofficial.history:
Produced at Manufacturing Plant SFF-IT1 on Itabaiana, the Hammerhead became a signature design for Clan Sea Fox with remarkable speed after its introduction in the mid-thirty-second century. Unusual in both appearance and philosophy among Clan designs, the 'Mech found immediate acceptance within the Sea Fox touman, where its durability and forgiving handling characteristics aligned well with the Clan's pragmatic approach to warfare. Clan Sea Fox offered the Hammerhead for export to all interested Clan buyers, and demand proved substantial. As Clans Jade Falcon and Wolf encountered opposing Hammerheads on battlefields across the Inner Sphere, both factions placed increasingly heavy orders of their own, feeding an escalating arms race in the years leading up to the ilClan conflict. Clan Ghost Bear developed a particular affinity for the design, admiring its resilience and unyielding nature.

Ghost Bear forces deployed numerous Hammerheads along their border with the Draconis Combine, where the 'Mech's ability to absorb punishment proved well-suited to defensive operations. During the Ghost Bear seizure of Lambrecht in 3150, elements of the Third An Ting Legion were brought from their posting on Ascella to reclaim the planet. A combat drop atop the Fifth Bear Guards was intended to scatter the defenders, but Ghost Bear forces held firm. A Star of Hammerheads and Ursuses withstood a charge from an entire company of An Ting BattleMechs, refusing to fall back and pinning the Kuritans in place until reinforcements could flank them.

The Hammerhead's influence extended beyond Clan Sea Fox's own production lines. Clan Wolf's development of the hundred-ton Amarok assault 'Mech drew direct inspiration from the Hammerhead's hulking arm design and hardened armor philosophy. The resemblance was close enough that Clan Sea Fox waged a series of Trials over what they considered design element theft, though the Wolves ultimately prevailed in these contests. Tensions between the two Clans over intellectual property did not prevent continued Hammerhead sales, however, as Clan Sea Fox proved willing to accept commerce even from rivals.

Clan Sea Fox also leveraged the Hammerhead's popularity to expand its commercial reach beyond Clan space. On Corey, Capellan authorities repeatedly rebuffed the Skate Khanate's attempts to establish trade relations, culminating in a confrontation in 3149 when Capellan aerospace fighters opened fire on a pair of Sea Fox Mule DropShips. The resulting batchall saw Hammerheads spearhead the assault on Capellan fortifications, tearing through defensive positions and pushing into the enemy's rear while heavier Stars exploited the breach. The engagement ended with Clan Sea Fox claiming the spaceport and surrounding facilities. The only persistent complaint regarding the design has been reports of occasional software glitches in exported models, which Sea Fox engineers attribute to conflicting software requirements from their diverse customer base.
BMHammerhead_2Unofficial.deployment: The standard Hammerhead configuration is the most widely produced variant and serves as the backbone of Clan Sea Fox's shock formations. Typically deployed in Stars alongside faster designs that can herd opponents into the Hammerhead's preferred close-range engagement envelope, the base configuration excels when used as the leading element in breakthrough operations. Its combination of heavy armor and stable firing platform makes it particularly effective in urban environments and confined terrain where enemies cannot easily disengage.

BMHoplite_HOP4CBATLCOS.overview:
The Hoplite was introduced in 2578 by Martinson Armaments of Terra as an infantry support BattleMech for the newly formed Star League Defense Force. Entering service during the opening battles of the Reunification War, the fifty-five-ton design proved itself a capable fire support platform, pairing a heavy autocannon with a long-range missile launcher to provide covering fire for advancing infantry formations. After a failed attempt to create a mainline combat variant, Martinson upgraded the electronics suite to produce the HOP-4C, though the design was ultimately relegated to Terran Hegemony militia commands by the twenty-seventh century.

Thought lost during the Amaris Crisis and early Succession Wars, the Hoplite survived among the SLDF exiles who would become the Clans, where its simple and rugged construction made it ideal for rapid production. The design later reappeared in the Inner Sphere in the hands of Wolf's Dragoons, raising immediate questions about the mercenary command's mysterious origins.
BMHoplite_HOP4CBATLCOS.capabilities:
Intended to operate in close coordination with infantry, the Hoplite sacrifices speed for firepower and protection. Its DAV 220 engine provides a maximum speed of only sixty-four kilometers per hour, making it one of the slower medium 'Mechs in service, but eleven and a half tons of DuraShield armor give it impressive staying power for its weight class. The primary armament of the HOP-4D centers on a Mydron Excel LB 10-X autocannon, capable of firing both standard and cluster ammunition, providing tactical flexibility against both hardened and dispersed targets. A Conan/5 LRM-5 launcher supplements the autocannon with long-range indirect fire capability, though the modest missile load requires careful ammunition management.

The Hoplite's design philosophy emphasizes reliability over sophistication. Sixteen heat sinks provide more than adequate cooling for its weapons loadout, and the standard fusion engine ensures the 'Mech can absorb significant punishment without catastrophic failure. However, the lack of jump jets and limited speed make the Hoplite vulnerable to flanking maneuvers, reinforcing its doctrinal role as a support unit rather than a frontline combatant.
BMHoplite_HOP4CBATLCOS.history:
The Hoplite's combat debut came against Taurian troops on Ridgebrook during the Reunification War, where its ability to absorb considerable punishment proved instrumental in anchoring SLDF infantry formations against determined Concordat counterattacks. Having demonstrated its effectiveness, the Hoplite became a common sight in 'Mech battalions assigned to infantry support roles throughout the conflict.

As the Reunification War dragged on, the SLDF's evolving tactical doctrine outpaced the Hoplite's capabilities. Increasingly advanced designs from the Terran Hegemony's factories saw the Hoplite redeployed alongside designs such as the Mackie and Banshee in Hegemony militia units, where it would suffer the heaviest casualties during the Rim Worlds Republic's seizure of the Terran Hegemony in the late twenty-eighth century. Martinson Armaments' factory on Terra was destroyed during the fighting in 2767, effectively ending Inner Sphere production.

The design survived among Aleksandr Kerensky's SLDF exiles, who valued its simplicity and ease of manufacture. When Nicholas Kerensky led his followers to Strana Mechty, the Hoplite blueprints were carried along, and an upgraded version (the HOP-4Bb) entered limited production at facilities on Strana Mechty and Eden in the years before the Pentagon Civil War. The Clans distributed the design among their toumans, though reactions varied considerably. The Snow Ravens rejected the Hoplite entirely due to its sluggish performance, while the Goliath Scorpions embraced its long-range capabilities.

Wolf's Dragoons selected the Hoplite for their journey to the Inner Sphere in 3005, believing the ancient design would avoid drawing attention. This calculation proved spectacularly wrong, as the appearance of a supposedly extinct 'Mech only deepened suspicions about the Dragoons' true origins. After cutting ties with the Clan Homeworlds in 3020, the Dragoons lost access to replacement Hoplites, and attrition steadily reduced their numbers. Following the Battle of Luthien in 3052, surviving Hoplites were refitted with salvaged Clan technology at Blackwell Corporation's facilities on Outreach, while experimental mixed-tech variants emerged from Arc-Royal MechWorks during the Jihad era.

By the Dark Age, Arc-Royal MechWorks had developed the HOP-5C, a cheap trooper variant using locally available materials to address Clan Jade Falcon's continued encroachment on the Arc-Royal Defense Cordon. Though never a prestigious design, the Hoplite's extraordinary longevity (spanning from the Reunification War through the ilClan era) stands as sign of the enduring value of simple, rugged engineering.
BMHoplite_HOP4CBATLCOS.deployment: This variant is the standard production Hoplite that served throughout the Star League era, differing from the original HOP-4A only in its upgraded Dalban HiRez II targeting and tracking system. Carrying the same Luxor HV AC/10 and Conan/5 LRM-5 combination as its predecessor, this variant was the variant most commonly encountered in Hegemony militia formations before the design's extinction in the Inner Sphere. These were also the first Hoplites seen in centuries when Wolf's Dragoons arrived in 3005, their presence among the mercenaries' forces immediately raising questions about the command's origins.
